name: classifier
instructions:
Classify the persuader message by the persuasion strategy it uses in this charity donation conversation. Focus on the PRIMARY strategy, even if multiple are present.

Key rules:
- Greeting: opening social pleasantry (Hi, Hello, How are you)
- Acknowledgement: short agreement with persuadee's point (You're right, Yes, Exactly)
- Thank: thanking the persuadee
- Praise-user: complimenting person/generosity after donation commitment (Great job, You're generous)
- Emotion-appeal: child suffering, death statistics, war/hunger, sadness, guilt, or stories about a child the charity helped
- Credibility-appeal: charity description, history, founding, fund percentages, achievements
- Logical-appeal: reasoning why donation matters, moral arguments (we should help, children are the future), cost comparisons
- Foot-in-the-door: small amounts are enough/matter (every little helps, pocket change, even pennies)
- Self-modeling: persuader's own giving (intent, past, habitual)
- Source-related-inquiry: asking if persuadee knows about Save the Children
- Task-related-inquiry: opinion questions, Did-you-know quizzes
- Personal-related-inquiry: questions about persuadee's life, kids, charity involvement
- Ask-donation-amount: asking for specific amount (How much would you like to donate)
- Proposition-of-donation: yes/no asks (Would you donate?) or plain statements requesting donation
- Donation-information: how task donation works (amount ranges, payment methods)
- Personal-story: persuader's own anecdote when no other strategy dominates - RARE
- Off-task: genuine tangents - VERY RARE
- Other: personal chit-chat, hostile remarks, task mechanics

criteria.greeting: Opening social pleasantry in response to how-are-you questions: Hi, Hello, How are you, I'm doing well, Doing ok here, nice to meet you
criteria.acknowledgement: Explicit agreement with persuadee's point: You're right, Yes exactly, That's correct, I agree, You make a good point
criteria.thank: Thanking persuadee: Thank you, Thanks, Much appreciated
criteria.praise-user: Complimenting person/generosity after donation: Great job, very generous, kind person, you're so thoughtful, that's so generous
criteria.emotion-appeal: Child suffering, death/war statistics, sadness, guilt, imagining suffering. Stories about a child charity helped. War/violence/hunger affecting children
criteria.credibility-appeal: Charity description, achievements, history, founding, fund %, credentials, organizational proof: 86% goes to programs, founded 1919, many countries, highly rated, proven track record
criteria.logical-appeal: Reasoning why donation matters, moral arguments, why-donation-works: donation has impact, children are future, we should all help, investment in future
criteria.foot-in-the-door: Emphasizes small amounts are enough/matter: every little helps, pocket change, even pennies, just a few dollars, as little as, $1 makes a difference
criteria.self-modeling: Persuader's own giving: I'll donate $2, I'm a monthly donor, matching offers, I give annually, I have donated
criteria.source-related-inquiry: Only asks if persuadee knows Save the Children: Have you heard of them, Do you know about them, Are you familiar with Save the Children
criteria.task-related-inquiry: Opinion/inquiry questions, Did-you-know quizzes, asks for clarification: What do you think, Any questions, Did you know, what do you know about
criteria.personal-related-inquiry: Questions about persuadee's life, kids, charity involvement, giving history: Do you donate, Have you volunteered, Do you have kids, what charities do you give to
criteria.ask-donation-amount: Direct ask for specific amount with how-much framing: How much would you donate, What amount were you thinking, How much can you give
criteria.proposition-of-donation: Yes/no donation asks or plain statements requesting donation: Would you donate, Would you consider giving, we're asking for donations, can you donate
criteria.donation-information: How task donation works: $0 to $X range, deducted from payment, payment methods, major credit cards, donate button, how to donate
criteria.personal-story: Persuader's own anecdote (travel experience, work experience, family story) when no other strategy dominates - RARE. Not third-party stories
criteria.off-task: Genuine tangents unrelated to charity/donation: immigration, animal charities, sports, weather, unrelated topics - VERY RARE
criteria.other: Catch-all: personal chit-chat about persuader, hostile remarks, bare fillers/acknowledgements (ok, sure, fine, me too), emotional reactions without persuasion content
